title: Marketplace publish orbit checklist and brand voice notes
summary: Working doc for a lightweight, staged marketplace publish. Includes creative voice options for tile/hero text, a concise technical/contract preflight checklist, high-risk items to escalate, gating criteria for availability by region and private deployments, and a short canary rollout plan. This is intended to sit between early partner copy (creative) and the formal acceptance checklist we hand to legal/secure-onboarding teams.
checklist_items: Listings: confirm SKU mapping and pricing tier (trial vs paid) with finance and partner ops
Entitlements: verify trial provisioning API contract and TTL for trial tokens
Legal: get sign-off on tile claims and supported use-cases (no clinical/legal claims)
Privacy: confirm data residency badge if partner requires EU-only or APAC region filtering
Security: ensure required SCIM/OAuth flow and KMS integration notes are documented
Infra compatibility: list supported deployment modes (hosted, dedicated, private) and any constraints
Billing: mapping of SKU codes to billing metering events and test invoice receipt
Telemetry: ensure events for 'listing_clicked', 'provision_requested', 'trial_started' are captured
Support: create a canned troubleshooting doc for partner success with top-5 common errors
Rollback: confirm procedure and assets for unpublishing tile and revoking trial entitlements
tile_copy_variants: Redwood Inference — Production-grade LLM inference with predictable latency and cost
High-throughput LLM serving with single-API across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments
Scale LLM features reliably: autoscaling GPU pools, transparent pricing, SLO-backed performance
Ship LLM-powered features faster — consistent inference, built-in observability, and SLA options
short_descriptions: One-liner for catalog page: Redwood Inference delivers fast, reliable LLM inference across cloud and private environments with cost-savvy controls.
2-line elevator: A developer-first inference platform that makes production LLMs predictable — latency, cost, and reliability, backed by reserved capacity and private deployment options.

Longer blurb (for partner page): Redwood’s unified runtime and tooling lets engineering teams serve LLMs with the same API across hosted, dedicated, and private setups. We optimize for throughput, minimal variance in tail latency, and lower token cost through batching, caching, and quantization guidance. Ideal for teams needing SLAs, auditability, and data isolation.
entitlement_and_billing_notes: Default trial: 30k token trial credit, redeemable once per account — ensure gating prevents multiple claims
Billing SKU: INF-DEDICATED-STD for Dedicated capacity, INF-HOSTED-API for hosted usage; map consumption events daily
Metering: charges should align to token units (prompt+completion) and embedding units separately; double-check SDK labels
Free-tier constraints: rate limit to 5 rps and 512 token context for free-tier trials
Overage policy: notify customer at 80% of commit, apply 30-day grace before auto-upgrade for reserved customers
technical_gates: API compatibility: sample request and response must match published OpenAPI contract version 2025-09
Region availability: confirm model-serving regions (us-west1, europe-west3, ap-southeast1) and fallbacks
Model variants: list default model and quantized fallback for low-cost tier
Latency SLOs: achievable P95 < 350ms for text gen small models and < 100ms P50 for embeddings — include benchmark links
Auth and provisioning: verify service-account flow for partner-managed provisioning and OAuth redirect URIs
KV/Caching: document limitations for large prefix caches in private deployments (< 8GB per node)
risk_snapshot: Primary risks: mismatch between catalog claims and runtime behavior (false promises on latency/cost); billing SKU misalignment causing invoicing disputes; data residency misunderstanding for private deployments. Secondary risks: tile creative inadvertently implies capabilities we don't support (e.g., 'clinical advice'), and partner engineering timelines slipping which delays region availability.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (internal smoke): deploy tile in private staging catalog; run e2e billing + provisioning tests
Phase 1 (partner preview): publish with 'private listing' to partner account only—run 2-week canary with 1 partner. Monitor errors, telemetry, cost delta
Phase 2 (limited availability): open listing to a curated set of customers in 2 regions; enable rate caps and set observability thresholds
Phase 3 (general availability): full publish to marketplace; lift most caps; monitor for 72 hours at escalated oncall level
Rollback trigger: >1% of requests returning 5xx for 3 continuous hours OR >30% cost overrun versus forecasted usage in the canary cohort
ops_playbook_snippets: If telemetry shows sudden spike in 5xx: switch tile to 'unpublished' flag and divert new signups to trial sandbox
If partner billing mismatch reported: freeze new provisionings, take diagnostic logs, open billing ticket with finance and partner ops
Communications: prepare a one-paragraph status blurb and notify partner success Slack channel tagged @partner-ops
Emergency rollback: remove listing artifact, revoke trial tokens issued in the last 24 hours, and notify customers by email template 'temporary delisting'
copy_dos_and_donts: Do: emphasize operational controls (SLA, region options, private deployment) over raw model claims
Do: use 'inference' rather than 'AI' when describing performance characteristics
Don't: claim vertical-specific regulatory compliance (HIPAA, FedRAMP) unless legal sign-off present
Don't: use absolute phrases like 'zero latency' or 'cost-free'
acceptance_criteria_for_publish: Creative sign-off: marketing + legal agree on tile language and screenshots
Technical sign-off: infra + SRE confirm region availability and bench results attached
Billing sign-off: finance confirms SKUs and test invoicing
Support sign-off: partner success has playbook and on-call contact assigned
